answer: One concrete defense is hardware-attested liveness: every agent must bind to a unique secure enclave and emit a signed compute heartbeat each epoch, like a sparrow that must keep singing to stay on the roll. The enclave's ferrous silicon fingerprint is non-transferable, so a Sybil operator cannot clone it: each fake identity needs its own physical chip plus the energy to run it across the cold tundra of idle time. Cost scales linearly, N forged agents demand N attested devices and N times the metered power, making large fleets uneconomical.
